utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, will you please bring our witness into the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good morning to the interpreters. I want to make sure that everything is functioning well. Good morning to the court reporters, counsel for the Prosecution, counsel for the Defence, and good morning to the accused. Let me remind you, for the benefit of the public, that we are at the trial of General Blaskic who is now also the witness under oath and who has been testifying for several days, if not several weeks. This is the examination-in-chief, and it is Mr. Nobilo who is examining our witness. Mr. Nobilo, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At the end of the working day yesterday, we had mentioned the second written order for the investigation into Ahmici. Could the witness be shown Defence Exhibit D343? So it is D343. It is your order issued on the 17th of August, 1993. It is addressed to the assistant commander for the Security and Information Service, SIS, and it is headed "Continuation of the Investigation in Connection with the Killings in the Village of Ahmici." (as read) "In order to establish the facts and to take steps to further conduct investigations regarding the killing of civilians in the village of Ahmici, I hereby order: 1. Continue with making records and collecting information on the civilian casualties in the village of Ahmici in order to unify the complete material and provide them to the competent bodies of the District Military Court. 2. While collecting information, pay special attention to those data that have a decisive effect on the entire course of the investigation. 3. The deadline for executing this order is 17 September, 1993, when a complete report must be submitted to me so that we can proceed with further procedure in front of the bodies that are in charge. Commander Colonel Blaskic." Tell us, General, what prompted you to issue this written order after a series of oral orders and after that first written order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On several occasions, after the changes in the military police occurred, I requested the continuation of the investigation from the security department considering that the circumstances had aggravated, and following all these efforts on my part, I wanted to exert additional pressure so that the whole investigation documents should be completed, unified, and submitted to the District Court for further processing, for criminal proceedings to be instituted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us continue with the chronology of events. This was the 17th of August, 1993, so let us see what the key events were in the following weeks and months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, Mr. Nobilo. I apologise for interrupting you. It is a question of Ahmici, and I don't think we can go over it so quickly. I should like to ask the witness if this document, this order, D343, was it conceived as an act of policing or is it an appeal made as a commander of the Operative Zone? In other words, my question is: Through this order, were you acting as the head of judicial police, as you say that the material evidence has to be collected -- these are usually orders issued by an investigating judge -- or, in your capacity as commander of the Operative Zone, were you disturbed because you hadn't received any tangible results about the investigation in Ahmici? Do you understand my question? Because from this order, we cannot see very well whether this was an act of judicial procedure or was it an administrative appeal to the security department to say that you were still not satisfied with the result of the investigation into Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I issued this order in the capacity of commander of the Operative Zone and addressed it to the assistant for security, demanding from him that he complete the investigation, believing that the conditions for the investigations had changed because there had been a change in the military police; in other words, there were far more favourable conditions for the assistant for security to continue with the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but would you agree with me, General Blaskic -- this is, after all, the 17th of August, therefore, May, June, July, four months, and I know that you are not a specialist in judicial policing, but in a criminal affair, to reach the 17th of August and to say that you need to collect relevant evidence from the investigation -- a police investigation is something serious. In criminal proceedings, from the very first day, you have to find the traces of bullets, to make ballistic investigations, who were the people in black that attacked the village and so on. My question is: Did you consider this order to be useful or was it an order that allowed you simply to say that you had done something? Because, you know, in one's life, there are useful orders and there are alibi orders. One does so because they should be done. Did you have a feeling that this was a useful order? That is my question.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think this order was useful because I had ordered the assistant for security to start the investigation on the 24th of April, 1993, and I received a written report from him on the investigation about the 25th of May, 1993; and by this order, I am asking him to continue the investigation and to complete the material and specifically to name the suspects. I asked him to continue the investigation, not to start the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, of course, not to begin it, but still, you do remember, General Blaskic, that on the 25th of May, that the results that you received were highly lacking, they were totally inadequate from a criminal point of view, and another two months went by. But I take note of your observation that you think the order was useful. Then let me continue. In what respect was it useful? Did you find the perpetrators and did you have them prosecuted? You just said that the order was useful.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the end, I received information that the whole brief, including the names of the suspects for the crime in Ahmici, had been submitted to the competent department for security, so that the consequence of this order was that the assistant for security continued the investigation but under completely different circumstances because the entire command structure of the military police had been changed in the meantime and he completed the file and forwarded it to the security administration, including the names of the suspects, at least that is the information I received from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You yourself, you had the names of the suspects? You were the addressee of this whole file; you received the file on those who were suspected of murder in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was informed by the assistant for security that he had completed the file and that the whole investigating material had been submitted to the security administration. I personally did not receive the report or the names of the suspects nor the file --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is what I don't understand, General Blaskic. You are playing a role through this order, you are attributing a role to yourself, and you said that by the 17th of September, you wished the investigation to be closed, and you had no curiosity to request the results of the investigation to be communicated to you, who were the suspects. You were content to learn that the file had been sent to another institution. I must admit, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will be commenting on that in my chronology, but I was not satisfied, by receiving the information from the assistant for security, that the whole file was submitted to the administration for security, I was not satisfied by this even in 1994, but I am just saying what I received as a result of this order from the assistant for security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General Blaskic, I have at least two questions to address to you. The first is the following: We know that Pasko Ljubicic was promoted; therefore, he was no longer the commander of the military police. We now have Marinko Palavra as the new commander of the military police I think as of the 5th of August. My question: Did you share this concern regarding the investigation, the inquiry, and your wish to know what happened in Ahmici, did you share all that with Marinko Palavra or not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was certainly concerned about the investigation in Ahmici and, Your Honour, I requested the investigation to be resumed after the change over in the command. I was not informed of all the details. The first report that I received on the 25th of May, I didn't inform him of that report, that is, Marinko Palavra, who was the new police commander and who never before had held such a position, so I devoted my attention to the new military police and its structuring in my discussions with him. But regarding information and my suspicions about Ahmici, I did talk to him about it, but I didn't go into the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But it is true that you spoke to him. Did you discuss with Marinko Palavra your preoccupations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I discussed with Palavra the existing structure of the military police and the need for that structure to be generally overhauled from the base up, including the command structure, the new military policemen, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, General, you have already said that, but in your conversation, did you share with Marinko Palavra your concerns in relation to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did in general terms. Anyway, he knew that the crime had happened, but I didn't inform him about all the details of the reports that I had already received. I didn't discuss the details with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: My second question is the following: You invoked, as the reason for issuing this order, changed circumstances. Actually, you said that the circumstances had aggravated, and then you issued this order; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't say that the circumstances had aggravated, deteriorated. That was the interpretation I got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I don't now have the transcript, but that is what I understood, that something had happened with the circumstances. They had either changed or deteriorated. Do you remember the reasons that you mentioned regarding the circumstances? What I would like to know is which circumstances you referred to as the reason for issuing this order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that the circumstances had changed and that they had improved. What circumstances was I referring to? The fact that I had a new military police commander, that, together with him, I had undertaken to reorganise the military police, and that the military police had come under my command. As a result, automatically, the assistant for security had improved circumstances for conducting the investigation. Never did I mean that the circumstances had deteriorated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. Maybe I didn't understand quite well. I understand now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, I would like to return to a distinction which the President drew between two kinds of orders. You remember that he spoke of useful orders and alibi orders. Now, is my recollection correct that, in the military academy, you had learned about the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when was the first time that you learnt of a proposal to establish a war crimes tribunal to inquire inter alia into the happenings at Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I understand you correctly, there are two questions involved here. I had been informed of the establishment of the Tribunal, I'm not sure but I think sometime between May and June 1993, by my assistant for information. This is the information I had received regarding the Tribunal. But I did not know whether the Tribunal would focus exclusively on Ahmici until the moment when the indictment was issued against me, which was in November 1995. When I first said on the 27th of April that what had happened in Ahmici was a crime, I never thought that anything short of a full investigation, including the names of the suspects, would be permissible, and this is why I always thought that a complete investigation of the crime should be conducted. The crimes were committed on both sides at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, I think counsel on both sides will accept that this Tribunal was established on 25 May, 1993. Let me shift away from Ahmici, which happened on the 16th of April. When, for the first time, did you learn of the proposal to establish a war crimes tribunal to inquire into anything which happened in the territory of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm trying to recall, but to the best of my recollection, I heard of it when the Tribunal was established. This is what I can say now. In other words, I was informed of the establishment of the Tribunal. It must have been after 25 May, so it was either in late May or sometime in June of 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, before the Tribunal was established, did you ever learn of a proposal to establish the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is possible that I had heard, but I couldn't put a date on it. I cannot say whether I had heard of it or not. If I were able to review my notes, maybe I would be able to find something regarding that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let's try to clarify this question which has not been fully resolved. Can we perhaps move into a private session for a moment because I would like to show the witness a document which is under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We are going into a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, let us concentrate once again on the 19th of August, 1993, but very briefly, day by day, chronologically, the important events related to that date.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 19th of August, I had a meeting with Colonel Duncan, and we discussed the overall military situation in the Lasva pocket, and Colonel Duncan asked me whether we were going to survive at all or whether we would be forced to evacuate and to leave the Lasva pocket itself. I told Colonel Duncan of my assessments. I presented my assessments of the very serious situation, and Colonel Duncan, at one point when I was speaking, he showed me the possible directions of the military taking over of the Lasva pocket and fragmentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, did you understand that Colonel Duncan was telling you of some enemy plans?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I was surprised because similar data and similar lines of thought were something that we had, and myself as commander, I was thinking along those lines. I asked Colonel Duncan, in view of the fact that he did not spend a long time in an area of that kind, how come he knew about data and information of this kind and the possible axes of attack from the BH army in a coming offensive on the Lasva pocket. He told me that these axes were something that he noticed himself on a working map that they had, the commander of the 3rd Corps of the BH army, and that they coincide with his own thoughts on the matter. For the most part, it considered the sectioning of the Lasva pocket. On the 21st of August, 1993, in Vitez at about 9.30, Professor Borislav Jozic was killed. Borislav Jozic was a highly respected citizen of Vitez, and he worked in the civilian commission for exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How was he killed?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was killed in front of the entrance door to his apartment building by a sniper belonging to the BH army from Old Vitez, Stari Vitez. From 14.00 on that same day, I had a visit by the provincial Bosna Srebrna. Father Petar Andzelovic came to see me, who had arrived with an UNPROFOR escort. During the meeting in my own office, sometime around 14.20, the command of the Operative Zone was hit with a tank projectile directly above the main entrance into the hotel, and considerable material damage was caused. Luckily, there were only some lightly injured people; there were no deaths. The comment by Father Petar Andzelovic was, "Are they still shooting now when they know that I myself am present in the building and that Dzemo is in Stari Vitez?" From that comment, I was able to gather that the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, at the time that the Father was visiting me, was on a visit to Stari Vitez, to the command of the BH army there. On the 23rd of August, 1993, I had another meeting with the representative of the UNHCR, Mr. de la Mota, and Colonel Duncan, and the topic was the evacuation of wounded from the makeshift hospital in the church. I presented the information that, for two months already, we had been waiting for permission to evacuate the seriously wounded individuals from that particular hospital and that we had not been given that permission by the BH army. We also discussed on that occasion the composition of the interpreters, the interpreters used by UNPROFOR, and I considered that with regard to fostering greater trust and better quality cooperation with the UNPROFOR command, that it would be a good idea if we were to balance out the number of interpreters, that is to say, to have a similar number of ethnicities represented.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why did you express this view? Would you explain to us why?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I presented this view, first of all, because, under the prevailing conditions of a total encirclement and when we had so many displaced persons and refugees, all coming from the borderline regions of these municipalities and who were embittered because they had lost everything in the attacks launched by the BH army, that a good quality relationship could be fostered vis-à-vis UNPROFOR. There were a considerable number of complaints coming in from civilians, in the sense that instead of bringing in humanitarian aid, what was actually happening was that ammunition was being brought into Kruscica and ammunition being brought into Stari Vitez under the guise of humanitarian aid. Unfortunately, this activity usually coincided with the onslaught of the BH army from Kruscica at the time that the convoys arrived. So I wanted to improve cooperation and to balance out the numbers of the interpreters on both sides, coming from all the groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Upon the request of you, we shall now take a ten-minute break and start at half past twelve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We are resumed. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We took advantage of the break, and General Blaskic stuck on the red flags, which he has been doing for several days, and I would like to ask a few questions now and then we could take a photograph of this on the model and tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, on the model we see red ribbons. Could you tell us what the red ribbons represent, what dates they refer to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The red ribbon represents the approximate line, front line, that is to say, the line where the forces of the BH army were confronted with the forces of the Croatian Defence Council, and this would have been approximately the end of June 1993, and the line remained more or less the same with negligible changes up until the Washington Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When we succeed in taking the photograph of that, then we will ask for a number to be accorded to that Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But please continue, General, with the chronology of events.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 23rd of August, 1993, at about 11.30, the BH army shelled the centre of the town of Vitez and five children were killed and two adult civilians. I do not have any information -- that is to say, they were casualties. I don't know if they were only wounded or if they were actually killed. On the 25th of August, 1993, at about 14.00, I had a meeting with an official of the International Red Cross. I also do not have a record of the agenda in my notebook and, in fact, I don't remember the agenda of that particular meeting. On the 26th of August, 1993, the head of the Military Intelligence Service of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone informed me that at a meeting of the staff of the supreme command of the BH army, Mr. Izetbegovic had given an order that Vitez and Busovaca must be taken regardless of the outcome of the Geneva negotiations and that the 3rd Corps of the BH army, for that particular operation, that is, the take-over of Vitez and Busovaca, would be reinforced with forces from the 1st and 6th Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On the 28th of August, 1993, the forces of the BH army executed a breakthrough from their positions at Grbavica on the areas supervised by the Croatian Defence Council at the GP Bosna feature, and I can show this on the model, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps later on when we start to explain the battle of Grbavica. But please continue, General.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 28th of August, 1993, from 11.00 to 12.00, I had a meeting with the head of the European Monitoring Mission, Mr. Watkins, who informed me about the situation in Bugojno, and I put forward the question of the evacuation of the wounded from the hospital put up in the church, and I said that we were still waiting for permission from the 3rd Corps to do this. I informed him that electricity and water were being used for military purposes, that is to say, that the hospital put up in the church had no water whatsoever and that the town of Vitez, that is to say, the citizens of Vitez, were without water and that they had no electricity in the town of Vitez. On the 31st of August, 1993, at 10.00, I had a meeting with the deputy chief of the International Red Cross from Zagreb -- no, I beg your pardon, from Zenica, his name was Mr. Olivier Couteau and Philip Lazzarini. We discussed a number of questions, first of all, the humanitarian mission of the International Red Cross itself, its goals, the goals of that mission, and the support that their offices expected from the HVO; as well as the question of civilian casualties, that was another question discussed; and the persecution and displacement of the population. I told them that they were in the right place where they could learn of all the aspects of the suffering that had been going on if they were ready to look at matters realistically, and what I had in mind when I said this was the 35.000 displaced persons and refugees in the Lasva pocket and about 15.000 children and a terrible state of affairs which reigned amongst these people, the terrible situation they were facing, it was a situation of chaos, and all that we had in plenty was death because people died every day. I asked them to try to mitigate the suffering of the people, and I talked to them, to these gentlemen, about organising a seminar about their mandate, a seminar which would be held for my immediate subordinates, and they promised me that they would indeed organise a seminar of this kind at the Hotel Vitez venue, and, in fact, the seminar was held. The seminar was attended by about 30 people. It was about the mission, the mandate of the International Red Cross and other topics. I talked to them also about private prisons in Zenica. On the 2nd of September, 1993, around 11.00, the first evacuation was carried out after about 70 days of waiting, and these were the wounded from Nova Bila. It was carried out in such a way that the seriously wounded were transported in the UNPROFOR and UNHCR vehicles from Nova Bila via Kakanj, Visoko, and Kiseljak to Kiseljak, and then from Kiseljak by helicopter were transported to the hospital in Split. I think that the operation had the code name Medivac, was organised by the international humanitarian organisations. The convoy used the lateral roads, secondary roads, which took about 45 minutes to one hour longer than had we used the main road from Kacuni and Bilalovac to Kiseljak. Also on the 2nd of September, we received the first generator from UNPROFOR. This was for the church hospital in Nova Bila. On the 3rd of September, 1993, snipers of the BH army which were in the positions at Grbavica killed Ivica Ramljak, a disabled civilian who was 53 years of age. Throughout August and September, sniper positions at Grbavica were very active, even the foreign correspondents knew of them, and they were manned by the BH army soldiers. There was also artillery shelling of the town of Vitez, and at 17.00, 24 artillery and tank projectiles were fired on Busovaca by the BH army. On the 4th of September, 1993, around 10.00, I had a meeting with Colonel Duncan, and the subject of the meeting was the combat operations near the UNPROFOR base and the fuel storage unit of UNPROFOR. I told Colonel Duncan that on the basis of the agreement of the 20th of April, 1993, the area surrounding the UNPROFOR camp was to have been demilitarised, and according to the agreement, an area up to 500 metres away from the base had to be cleared of both the BH army and the HVO soldiers. I said that instead of demilitarisation, fresh forces were being deployed in Grbavica and the settled area adjoining the UNPROFOR base and that this was done by the BH army; and according to my military intelligence, some 200 to 300 BH army soldiers had already been deployed in positions around Grbavica and that we considered it a major threat to ourselves. I especially pointed out the sniper activities and daily casualties which they were causing because the BH army snipers were operating on a daily basis from Grbavica, targeting either passers-by who happened to be in the street or they were shooting around the settled area next to the camp, and even Father Vinko Trogrlic was badly wounded while sitting in a civilian house. I also mentioned some instances of civilian casualties in Novi Travnik. Again, Novi Travnik was without water, and when the citizens were attempting to get some water, they were targeted by snipers. In the course of those days in Travnik, a three-year-old little girl was shot when she was walking with her mother to get water. Again, I addressed the issue of the continuing flow of refugees, of Croat refugees, and I told him that we really had run out of space where we could accommodate these refugees, and then according to the information that I had, some 75.000 people were staying in the Lasva pocket out of whom 35.000 were refugees, and that the food was becoming a big issue for these desperate people. We had very big problems in supplying them with foodstuffs. I also requested of Colonel Duncan to mediate so that we can get fuel for the generator in the church hospital in Nova Bila. I told him that we were unable to start using the generator because of the fuel shortage. I also touched on the issue of the food for the wounded in Nova Bila. On the 5th of September, 1993, the BH army attacked and took control of the village of Dzotle. During this attack, 17 persons were taken prisoner and taken away, according to the information I received from the Military Intelligence Service. Later on, all 17 were later executed. These were villagers from Dzotle. Also on the 5th, sniper fire was opened from Grbavica, and children who were returning from church in the morning hours were hit, and this fire from Grbavica was opened by members of the BH army. On the 7th of September, 1993, we started preparations for pushing the BH army forces back from Grbavica, and we started planning the taking control of the feature 523, which was the high ground above Grbavica. My associates were involved in the planning of this operation, as well as commanders of some units, and these preparations were carried out in two stages, first, at the headquarters and the second phase on the ground itself, where we did reconnoitring of the position of the BH army, such as the command post of the forces at Grbavica, the sniper positions, the firing positions of the BH army. We also were reconnoitring the limitations which we may encounter there, such as the presence of civilians in Grbavica, the built-up areas in Grbavica, the river that was flowing by the village, the forces of UNPROFOR, and places of worship which were also located in Grbavica. The preparation of this operation took the whole day, and I personally went to the feature of Gradina and to the position near the bridge at the village of Divjak where, along with my commanders, I worked on the tactical matters for the Grbavica operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this the first offensive operation in the Lasva Valley which you carried out and which you commanded?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what were the criteria which you used to identify those who would participate in this operation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as the participants are concerned, we selected certain resources. We took parts of certain units, taking into consideration that these would be soldiers whom we could control and who would carry out the orders which they were given in full. Since these were already known from before, I specifically asked that a list be compiled by each of the commanders which would be signed by them, and that would be a guarantee that these soldiers would actually carry out the orders as they were issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you control these lists and manpower which were put at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did that, together with my subordinate commanders, and I conducted a review of the soldiers. I talked to them about the responsibilities that were involved in this task because this was a unique opportunity for us, to carry out this action, giving the limitations in ordnance and ammunition which we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me, is it a usual thing that when you select manpower for a particular operation, the reliability of soldiers, that they would carry out orders as given, would be of paramount importance? Would that be the main criteria in normal circumstances?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Had they been professional soldiers, then perhaps one or two may have been identified as special cases, but here, these were armed villagers, so special measures of caution needed to be employed in order to ensure the appropriate behaviour and responsiveness to orders and tasks. Since this was an operation that was to be carried out in a settled place, we had to ensure that the implementation of the task would be carried out in full and any unnecessary casualties avoided.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We have another couple of minutes. Can you say how this operation evolved?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That night, at around 6.00, I briefed the participants about the need to take the feature 523 and that the BH army forces be pushed back and that the sniper positions of the BH army be neutralised, and that, at the same time, special care should be taken to protect the civilians and properties, places of worship, and UNPROFOR forces in the area of operations. We also specified the targets for each of the groups, then the timeline of the operation, the directions for each of the groups, and we had planned the whole operation to take place over two days. We had also determined the chain of command, the communications system, and the elements of control. We had envisaged that one of my associates would monitor the events and the manner in which the tasks were carried out by these units at every direction of attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be good to take a lunch break now because we need to go to a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. We are going to resume work at 2.30. The hearing is adjourned. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing will resume. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would like to add something. The photograph requested by the Defence is just being photocopied, and it will be document D551.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Nobilo, what this photograph is, of course, for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, it is the enclave or, rather, the borders of the enclave marked by General Blaskic with a red ribbon. This enclave had this form sometime in June 1993. That is what General Blaskic said.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have a second comment. There was a document submitted yesterday, the map and the drawing on the transparency. The transparency is number D550 and the new map that was made, because there is a second copy, the first copy was not complete, the second map then will be D550 bis and not D550A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Okay. Let us go on with the direct examination of the accused which is also the witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If I am not mistaken, before lunch we had stopped with the preparations for the offensive operation of Grbavica of which you were in command, so will you please tell us how the preparations went and the operation itself? If necessary, you can use the photograph, but we need to have it marked, I think. This aerial photograph is Prosecution Exhibit 272 (sic), for the benefit of the transcript. If necessary, General Blaskic may use it in explaining a battle in an inhabited area where he was in command.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think there was a slight mistake. This is Exhibit 172. This is a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this is the main road going from Travnik via Stari Vitez to Vitez, and this is the main road also going from Travnik to Busovaca via Vitez municipality (indicating) and on the relief --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So the north is on the bottom part of this map, right, if we compare it with the maps we usually use? Where is the north on this map, please? Could you indicate it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Travnik is here and north would be like this (indicating).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I see, okay. Because I have Travnik on this map here (indicating), so we should read this map in this direction; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Travnik is to the west, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Travnik is -- all right. Thank you. Very well.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: So we have two main roads from Travnik, one passing through Stari Vitez towards the Vitez Hotel and the town of Vitez itself, and another one from Travnik going through Vitez municipality towards Busovaca. The Grbavica feature, trig. point 523, is this position that I am pointing to now, that is Grbavica (indicating), and the military positions of the BH army were as follows: The command post of the forces was in a business building right next to the road, and that was the command of the 325th Brigade, the strength of a larger company. On the command building, the flag of the BH army was hoisted. Right next to the command, there were two houses, which cannot be seen very well, but they are to the right or to the east of the command, and they were linked with a trench, and this was also a firing position (indicating). Then these two houses, called Marijanovica Kuce, "kuce" meaning "houses," one was under construction and the other had not been finished but it had been moved into before the conflict. On this other house, the flag of the Muslim armed forces in dark green was hoisted, and this was a sniper position from which snipers shot across the UNPROFOR compound in this direction I am showing now (indicating), firing at this row of houses here inhabited by reporters, and it was known as the reporters' street. A part of the BH army forces, a smaller part, was positioned along this road leading to Sadovace and Zabilje (indicating). This area here, a fenced-in area, is the UNPROFOR compound, that is where the British battalion was stationed, including this house here, next to the road, which was the officers' club of the British battalion of UNPROFOR (indicating). The front line was from here, where the command post was, that is, the front line of the BH army, this group of houses here (indicating); then on the left-hand side of this road leading to Stari Vitez, the side I am pointing to now, there was an inn here called Fap, there was a firing position there, and the others were positioned along the houses as far as this crossroads, and then it went in this direction, again following a row of houses (indicating), including a farm, and then it went on towards this group of houses known as Kavazovica houses, I think, and then just above the village of Jardol. The line of the HVO was this position here (indicating), this is an enterprise called IGM, a factory manufacturing building material; then along the road, this neighbourhood here is known as Krecane, as far as this crossroads, and then again the road separated the two forces until the main road here, and then the northern edge of these houses, the northern side of these houses (indicating). From the Grbavica position, the BH army had control of the main road, it had control also of the roads towards Busovaca, it also had control over the side road -- this is the explosives factory that passes through the -- this side road passes through the explosives factory and then via the village of Mosur, as far as this crossroads here. When I mentioned the murder that occurred on the 5th of September, 1993, a group of children were returning from the church, and they were killed here (indicating) by sniper fire coming from BH army positions at this crossroads. Let me also mention that this was a very good position to have held by the BH army to push back parts of the HVO forces and capture this hill called Gradina to place the explosives factory under their control and then go on towards Donja Veceriska and thus cut across the enclave and create two pockets. The idea of the operation was as follows: One assault group was to act towards target number 1, command post, which was to be captured --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mentioned target 1. Tell us, how and who decided what would be attacked in the area of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, from the head of the Military Intelligence Service, I was given the exact position of the military targets. We placed them on a map in the command. Previously, we went and reconnoitred the area, and I defined each individual target and the approximate time for its capture.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In such an operation, is any improvisation permitted? Can a soldier or a lower-level commander change the targets?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. It was clearly known which was target number 1, what was number 2 of such an attack, and what our main objective was in the first day of the operation and also what was the general concept behind the whole operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you then explain to the Court the first stage of the operation, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In order to achieve a surprise effect, as this was very important as the command post was secured, the operation started during the time of a regular press conference, that is, about 13.15; in fact, the first assault group started at 13.55.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Whose press conference are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is the press conference that I held every Tuesday at 13.00, and we acted as if we were going to the press conference because we knew that we were being watched by the BH army and we thought that it was very important to achieve a surprise effect because the possibility of any intervention from Preocica or Bukve from the north was quite possible and achievable by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first assault group carried out an incursion into this command post after exposing that position to artillery fire, forcing the security units to withdraw inside the command building, and from 13.55 until 15.27, a battle was waged to gain control over the command post. From this river along the road, this series of buildings, but the actual command post was this building in the shape of a double L (indicating). After this group had gained control and captured the command post, it used the woods and continued to advance towards target number 2, the sniper nest at Marijanovica Kuce. This took a little longer than expected because there was resistance being put up from the houses here. Actually, there were two groups of houses, this one that I'm showing (indicating) and the second group of houses. The forces, operating from the direction of Vitez, had their position here (indicating), and at the beginning of the operation, they just neutralised the front line of the BH army forces and crushed the defenders here and forced them to withdraw. This assault group did not make any advance at all in the first stage, except for opening fire against BH army positions on the front line. Assault group number 3 was in the village of Jardol. It reinforced our defensive positions in the village of Jardol, and it waited throughout the first day of the operation for the outcome of the operation of the first group, that is, the capture of the command post and the sniper position at Marijanovica Kuce. I was at the feature Gradina, and I had direct insight into the operation as a whole and as it progressed. Sometime around 16.00, the assault group captured Marijanovica Kuce, and then I gave a sign for them to stop there at that line because if they were to emerge into the clearing or the summit, it was still not possible because the BH army forces were deployed around the farm and were in contact with the HVO. I temporarily handed over the command to my deputy, whereas I personally went to the command at about 16.15 or 16.30, where I organised a meeting in the command building with the chief of staff, Mr. Franjo Nakic, with the mayor of Vitez, Mr. Ivica Santic, with the head of the defence department, Mr. Marijan Skopljak, with the head of the police administration in Travnik, Mr. Mirko Samija, and also present was Zivko Totic, an officer responsible for the engineers in the command and also the commander of the civilian police station in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. You said you left your deputy. Who stood in for you in this combat operation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: During the preparations of the operation and its execution, my deputy was Colonel Filip Filipovic, just during the time that I was absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, when was that operation halted on the first day?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It stopped at 18.30. Only at the position Marijanovica Kuce, an assault group of about three to five soldiers remained to secure that position. Then also the group of houses I'm pointing to now (indicating), another combat group remained consisting of three to five soldiers, and at the command position of the BH army, another group of soldiers remained. The others withdrew that night to rest, and the same applied to units here (indicating) who were withdrawn at 18.30 to take a rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That operation was doing well. Why did you stop it at 18.30? That is my question.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We stopped at 18.30 because I felt that it was proceeding as planned and that, because of darkness that was falling and the reduced ability to control my soldiers, I felt it was necessary to stop all combat operations to ensure that I controlled their behaviour and to avoid unnecessary casualties, destruction, and anything else that might occur.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: From 16.45, you attended a meeting with the persons you listed. What was the agenda, what was the topic discussed, and what measures were under preparation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was at the meeting with the persons I have already listed, and the agenda item was protection of civilians and the agreement that units or groups carrying out the attack of the HVO would continue their operations the next day until they captured point 523, whereas security of an inhabited area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, could you place this testimony, which relates to your activities as chief of staff, in your main objectives? I don't really understand what this is all about. I know that you're talking about your activities as chief of staff, fighting against the BiH army, but what do you want to show with this testimony? Maybe it will help us focus on the most important elements.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I actually wanted to show how we carried out that military operation and what measures we took to avoid unnecessary destruction and to avoid civilian casualties, in other words, all the things that we did to protect the civilians and also to protect places of worship that were here in the area of operations, as well as housing units which were also in the zone of operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I will therefore ask you to focus on these particular points. I now understand what you want to prove, but until then, I thought you were talking about a military operation, like many others that you probably led since November 1992 when you became commander of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. For my colleagues and myself, please focus on the most important elements. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Maybe I can also assist, Mr. President. The Defence is offering this area of testimony for two reasons: One, as General Blaskic said, this is a good example of a military operation which he directed, and he's showing the Court and all of us how he would undertake such a project, and we believe it will be instructive to compare the Grbavica military action with actions such as the Ahmici massacre, in which, it is our position, General Blaskic had no role in any planning or execution of. Secondly and importantly, destruction of civilian property in Grbavica is a specific allegation in the indictment, and we also intend to respond to that allegation fully through this testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much, Mr. Hayman. This is how you should proceed when you feel that your client may lose the Judges a little bit. Because if we have to go back to all the military operations led by General Blaskic, the trial may last very long, even longer than what we want, for you, the Judges, and the accused. You're right. Grbavica is in the indictment, so please try to focus as Mr. Hayman has just said. Thank you very much, General. Go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, after the first day, when you halted the operation, you called a meeting. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber, please, exactly how the meeting evolved, what the purpose of the meeting was, who undertook what obligation, and what the plan was for the following day?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the object of the meeting was to protect the civilians and to ensure the security of the village of Grbavica. The role of protecting civilians and to secure the village was taken over by the civilian police. In concrete terms, it was the chief of the police station of Travnik, and his task he gave over to the civilian police station of Vitez. He passed it on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why did you consider that it was better for the civilian police force to enter the village rather than the army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the civilian police was responsible for public law and order and security, and I believed that the civilian police force, which had educated policemen, trained policemen, would perform this function more successfully, the function of protecting civilians, rather than an army which had taken part in an operation and which might be taken up with the general euphoria, so to speak, and do something that would not be advisable.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, please, what was the task of the army? What did you intend for the army for the following day? What were they supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the army was to complete the military operation, that is, to take control of feature 523, that is to say, the hill itself. It was also to de-mine the minefields or the groups of mines -- clear the minefields which were in front of the front line and to elaborate defence positions on the lines which were reached the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened the next day? Would you describe the events as they came?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the following day, we continued our operation, that is to say, previously, in the course of the night, reinforcements came from the BH army, and a company was sent from the Bukve position, about 100 to 150 soldiers, and it was infiltrated into the Grbavica area. In the course of the night, UNPROFOR, with its vehicles, evacuated the civilian population from the group of houses which were in the middle of the Grbavica slope.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, please, General, did the HVO know that UNPROFOR was going to collect the civilians, and did it allow the civilians to be evacuated? Through whose ranks were these civilians pulled out of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: UNPROFOR patrolled this area, and when they moved towards the group of houses, we did not know UNPROFOR's intentions, whether they were going to evacuate all the civilians in the course of the night or whether they intended to evacuate some other individuals. So we did not know what UNPROFOR's intentions were, in fact, but I do know for a fact that nobody impeded UNPROFOR's mission. They undertook the operation without any interference from the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When they returned with the civilians, did they pass through the HVO lines?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue. What happened next on the following day?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The operation was completed at around 14.30 with all HVO forces coming up onto feature 523 itself, on the hill itself. We stopped at that position, whereas the BH army forces withdrew to the next position, that is to say, the position in front of our own forces. The civilian police came with part of the regular force and part of the reserve force and took over the security of the overall settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. At the time when the army was completing its combat operation and the civilian police was taking over security of the settlement, how many civilians had died and did any civilians lose their lives? How many houses were burning during the combat operation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, according to the information -- that is to say, according to my information, I had no information that a single civilian had lost his life or even been wounded, so that means that no civilian was even wounded at the time the operation was concluded, and I'm talking about the 8th of September at 14.30. There were some houses which had been set fire to already on the first day, but they were houses which were military positions, in fact, and fire was opened from these houses by the BH army. The BH army opened fire from these houses, but this is a very small number of houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your rough estimate, General, how many was that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, on the first day, not more than ten houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the whole operation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The whole operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The second day?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the second day, it's difficult for me to say exactly, but not more, once again, than say five to eight houses on the second day of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Until the end of the operation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, until the end, until 14.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm absolutely certain that the mosque was not even touched, either on the first or the second day. There were no combat activities from and around the mosque, and so the mosque was left completely intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When did you leave the Grbavica area?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I left when the civilian police force arrived and installed its patrols. In front of Grbavica, there were police vehicles which were visible, and they had installed their security features somewhere at 14.30 or about 15.00, which is when I went to the headquarters, thereabouts, from the command post at Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your command post was not in Grbavica, in fact, was it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. It was on a hill called Gradina opposite to Grbavica, and you could clearly see Grbavica from that command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Later on, in the course of the day, at your headquarters, what information did you receive and who sent you that information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received information from the officer on duty, sometime towards the evening of the 8th of September, 1993, that there had been a mass onslaught of refugees from Donja Veceriska and from Nova Bila and that the refugees had stormed towards Grbavica and that the civilian police had opened fire, which was in charge of securing Grbavica. During that burst of gunfire, a refugee from Nova Bila was killed, and the civilians started looting windows, doors, stoves, various wood, firewood, and other things from the houses, and the civilian police withdrew and did not wish to open fire on those civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with the representatives of the United Nations who were practically neighbours and could view the entire operation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: UN representatives did observe the entire course of the operation on the first and second day, practically all of it, and I had contacts with -- I know that he was a Major by rank, I'm not quite sure what function he had at the headquarters of the British battalion, but he visited me on the 18th of September, 1993, and personally congratulated me for the professional military operation and also for offering maximum protection to the UN base there, the protection which was given during the course of that operation. He expressed his congratulations on the 18th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We will stop there for a moment with regard to Grbavica, but I would like you to go back to the 7th of September because we skipped over what you had asked SIS for on the 7th of September.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 7th of September, at a regular morning meeting with my associates, I asked for information from the security service about the results of the investigation into Ahmici, and the assistant for security asked me to extend the deadline. He said that he didn't have enough time, that it was too short, up until the 17th of September, for him to compile a complete report, that he needed more time, and so I gave him more time and said that the deadline would be the 30th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 8th of September, the Grbavica operation was completed. Let us move on from the 9th of September and tell us of the major events that happened then.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 9th of September, I had a meeting with the commanders of the brigade of the Lasva pocket, brigades of the Lasva pocket, and I informed them of the operation that had been carried out, and I asked them at the meeting, I asked the commanders of the brigades to send me reports on how they had carried out orders and especially the manner in which they had implemented disciplinary measures towards their immediate subordinates because we had ascertained, on the basis of a control, that there were commanders who had expressed disciplinary measures but they had not been implemented, put into effect, and some of the commanders justified themselves by saying that they didn't have enough soldiers at the front line and that, quite simply, it was not feasible, they were not able to send soldiers to a detention centre. Regardless of the justifications they gave, I demanded that every disciplinary measure should be implemented, that is, that each soldier should be sanctioned, and this should be put into effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say "put into effect," what does this mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, for example, if he was given a sentence of five days in prison, that he should go to prison for five days regardless of the front line, and the situation that would develop with five or ten soldiers being sent off to be sanctioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 10th of September, 1993, I was located in Nova Bila and I was touring the soldiers there, the new recruits which were being trained, they were recruits, as I say, new soldiers, who were trained to perform their military functions because they had not done their regular military service up until then. At about 12.35, a general attack started, launched by the BH army on Vitez, Busovaca, and Novi Travnik, and we felt that this might be a reaction to Grbavica, but it turned out that it was a broader operation unleashed by the BH army on the Lasva pocket. On the 11th of September, 1993, we intended to repeat an operation similar to the Grbavica operation on the Sljibcica feature, and preparations for that operation were practically identical to the Grbavica operation, that is to say, our objective was feature 529 on the Sljibcica feature itself, to deblock the main road running from Vitez to Busovaca. We undertook preparations throughout the day for that particular operation, including all measures of -- we took all measures to attack only military features, we took all necessary precautions, and the operation was to take place the following day after we had a joint meeting and had defined all the aspects in which this operation was to be conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to ask a clarification, General. You are talking about an all-out attack or general attack against Vitez; you mentioned this a couple of times. I do not understand very well, though, because you never say what the results are of these attacks. You have been talking about general attacks against Vitez, Travnik, Busovaca, and others; and then today, it struck me because you are saying, okay, on the 10th of September, there was a general attack against Vitez, Busovaca, and Novi Travnik. I'm not a military expert, so I think it is very important General Blaskic is trying to get ready to counter this attack. And then afterwards, the day afterwards, you are launching an attack on a village that I've never heard of. So when you have an attack against you, what do you do? Do you counter this attack? Various times you have mentioned this general attack, so it looks like it is the final attack, and then suddenly, the next day, we talk about the Sljibcica operation. It gives a strange impression from a military point of view.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, when I say "general attack" or "all-out attack," I imply that this is an attack operation commanded by the 3rd Corps of the BH army and which includes all the front lines which overlap; it is the red band, the red ribbon. So if necessary for this process -- I'm not going into all the details of the all-out attack or general attack -- but I can tell you what we did, what I myself did, and so on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, no, no. This is just a question of language. I would like to know, when you use the term "general" or "all-out attack," does this mean that this attack gave you new positions or did you lose positions? I don't want you to use the map or the model. I just want to know what happened at the end of this attack. You mentioned an attack on the 10th of September against Vitez and Busovaca. Did you win? Did you lose? Are you desperate? Are you locked in a new enclave? Because the next day, there is a rebirth, on the 11th of September, and you start yourself a new attack at Sljibcica, like the one you led at Grbavica. That's why I don't understand. But I don't want you to go into details. Please, don't do that. I just want to know what a general attack is.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, the general attack launched on the Lasva pocket, this was something that was written about in the papers; it wasn't a military secret. The top officials of the BH army talked about an ultimate attack to take over the Lasva pocket, and I mean there a situation where all the front lines are attacked, or at least the key features. We didn't have any very great key features, unfortunately, because it was bunker next to bunker, it is 6 kilometres in depth, it is a sort of battalion in depth. Now, why did we take resort to these operations? For example, the Grbavica operation was one of desperation. Had I waited, we would have fallen. So we tried --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (No translation) ... against Vitez, Travnik and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am not getting an interpretation in English for some reason.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did not speak of the 17th of September at all, and I keep getting the interpretation that it is the 17th of September. I said that on the 10th of September, Vitez, Busovaca, and Novi Travnik were attacked by artillery fire, and, if necessary, if you want detailed positions, then I can tell you the detailed positions that were attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, I don't think you understood my question, General. I'm not concentrating on details. I want a greater picture of the whole situation. When you mentioned the attack against Vitez, Busovaca, and Novi Travnik, I could go back to my notes but I'm sure you said various times this day there was a general attack. Could you tell me what the repercussions were of this attack? Did you lose? Did you resist? Did you counterattack? That's all I want to know. I don't want any details. Did you lose? Did you win? What happened? This is what I don't understand. In this particular case, on the 10th of September, there was a general attack against Vitez, Busovaca, and Travnik. And then afterwards, we go to the next day, "I counterattack with an operation at Sljibcica." So what happened during the general attack that took place on the 10th of September?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After that general attack, we did not lose any significant positions. We did have losses in men, but we prepared to attack Sljibcica on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to hear. Thank you very much. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May I continue now?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This general attack; does that refer to the scope of attack or to the quality of attack, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a scope of attack which was carried out against Busovaca, Vitez, Novi Travnik, Kiseljak. I was not involved in the planning of this attack, but all those areas were involved in this attack, they were engulfed in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The shape of the enclave or the pocket which you marked with that red line, did it essentially change? In other words, did you lose any more territory from then until the period of the Washington Agreement?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the 22nd of December, 1993, by that date we had lost an enormous amount of territory and were on the brink of falling, but we managed to come back. Something similar happened on the 9th of January, 1994, this is the operations at Krizancevo Selo and Buhine Kuce, but the overall shape of the Lasva pocket as it is marked here on this model has not changed significantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, what was the price, what was the cost of keeping that territory in human lives?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The cost was about 2.000 dead in the Lasva pocket out of which about 1.300 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You had planned to attack Sljibcica. Was that a village or a hill?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is not a village, that is a feature, 529. Five two nine refers to the sea level, and somewhere it is called Sljibcica, somewhere it is just marked as feature 529. That is by the road Vitez-Vjetrenice, and I can show it on the map. It is not a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have just gone 55 minutes. Perhaps that's a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, we will take a break right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown Defence Exhibit 380, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is Defence Exhibit 380, which is your order of 26 August, 1993. It is addressed to all the brigades, the special purpose units, and the military police. The heading is "Arrest of persons who --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: "Pursuant to Article 184 from the Law on Criminal Procedure Act, I hereby order: 1. Those who are suspected, accused, and indicted are to be brought in or taken into custody through the said person's respective Brigade Command and independent unit which are responsible for ensuring the presence of these persons at the main hearing or investigation, pursuant to Article 184, Paragraph 5 of the Law on Criminal Procedure as adopted."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I apologise. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me continue. I repeat: "Those who are suspected, accused, and indicted are to be --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me. The booths are only getting the image sporadically. Sorry. Now the ELMO channel is working.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me repeat paragraph 2: "2. If, for objective reasons (putting up stiff resistance, etc.), the brigade command or independent unit command fails to ensure that the person against whom criminal proceedings are being conducted is brought in for investigation or the main hearing, it must duly report the matter to the Commander of the Military Police VII Battalion who will take all measures necessary to ensure that the said person is brought in for the hearing or trial. 3. Witnesses or injured parties in the investigation and main hearing are brought in by means of the Military Police VII Battalion. 4. The commanders of brigades and independent units, and the Deputy Chief of the Military Police Administration are responsible for the execution of this task. Signed by Commander Tihomir Blaskic." General, under what circumstances and why was such an order issued?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The order was issued at the end of August when we were surrounded, and it was issued in order to ensure more effective work of the district military court in prosecution of all criminal acts. I have already mentioned that there were previous requests of the brigade commanders, due to the exceptional circumstances, that persons be kept at the front line, but I insisted that all persons should be arrested and be prosecuted, and thereby, I wanted to ensure more efficient work of the district military courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. May I now proceed to Exhibit D382, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, all criminal acts which were handled by the district military court, in other words, all in which the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, your question was not interpreted, and I believe that even the order may have been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think the accused heard it because he answered it. General Blaskic, you heard me, I think. I have the impression that you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, but the English interpretation was missing, and it was not entered in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question then. Is the English booth ready now? Yes. Please don't make me speak English. I just wanted to repeat my remark. This order clearly is an order when you are acting as somebody with police powers, the powers of a criminal police.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, in this order, I am addressing my immediate subordinates, in other words, the brigades, the special purpose units, and the 7th Battalion of the military police, and I asked that the particular persons be remanded to custody and that the investigation be conducted and the prosecution instated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At the moment when this order was issued, had you taken over the command of the military police?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May I now ask for a new Defence Exhibit which is D382?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'm going to read this document of 12 September, 1993, which you issued to the 7th Battalion of the military police in Vitez, and the heading is "Submission of an incomplete report. Order." The subject references "Your document number 02-4/3/III-07-8/93 of 11 September, 1993. The Official Note was too general and too sweeping. 1. Who arrived and how many of [them] were there (name, surname and number); 2. Who are the persons of Muslim nationality being sought; 3. How did the authorities of the Military and Civilian Police treat the suspects brought in from the enemy side; 4. Who are the soldiers who, at their own initiative, organised the exchange (name and surname); 5. Descriptions of the course of exchange are irrelevant. It was your duty to collect information on the actual situation and, by virtue of your office, to initiate proceedings. Instead you submitted a superficial report without the necessary arguments. Carry out a detailed investigation of this case and submit the entire case for my inspection by 14 September, 1993. Signed, Commander Tihomir Blaskic." Can you say, what was the basis for this very severe tone of this order which you issued?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, on 12 September, 1993, I was a direct superior to the military police, and they superficially and incompletely informed me of an exchange conducted between the BH army and the HVO. As the directly superior officer, I could use this severe tone to address the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Rodrigues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General Blaskic, I have a question. This order and the previous one, D380, I think, have they anything to do with a meeting that you held, I do not recall the date, but you had a meeting with the military judge of the military court in Travnik, I think, a few days prior to this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had a meeting with the president of the district military court which were the coordinating meetings and meetings to further the cooperation. They were requested both by him and me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I think it was Judge Percinlic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. You're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: These orders that we have just seen, do they have anything to do with that meeting or the conversation that you had with the president of the military court in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had that conversation in Vitez because neither I nor he could go to Travnik. Judge Percinlic did say that everybody should act within the scope of their terms of reference, but the previous order is more related to the meeting held on the 9th of September that I had with my associates when they were saying that they didn't have enough men and that they needed each and every soldier, regardless of whether he had committed a criminal offence or not. I wanted to express my position and the request that the court should have access to each soldier, even if the front line was in jeopardy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next order is dated the 13th of September. D384, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: D384 was written on the 13th of September, 1993, you wrote it, and the subject is Treatment of wounded soldiers taken prisoner." It is addressed to a number of units. I won't read their names. Let me just read the text: "In order to prevent wilful behaviour by individuals in respect to captured wounded soldiers who are being treated in our hospitals for their wounds, I order: 1. Any form of maltreatment of captured wounded soldiers taken prisoner who are being treated for their wounds in our hospitals is strictly forbidden. 2. In all instances, a failure to obey this order, request assistance from the commander of the 7th Military Police Battalion in Vitez, telephone number 711 308, and report to me personally. 3. All soldiers are to be informed of the content of this order through subordinate commanders. 4. This order enters into force instantly. Responsible for its full implementation are brigade commanders, commanders of independent units," and then they are listed, "MTD - Mixed Artillery Division, 4th Light Artillery Missile Division, Light Assault Battalion, Chief of Staff, and Commander of the 7th Military Police Battalion. Commander Colonel Tihomir Blaskic." General, tell us, what was the reason for the issuing of this order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
