utterances.text: It was protection and humane treatment of captured and wounded soldiers who were being treated in the church-cum-hospital, and I remember that at one point, there was some reaction because this was a makeshift hospital, in fact, a church, in which certain groups of soldiers, when learning that a captured soldier of the BH army was being treated there, would try to resort to violent acts, and I tried to prevent that. Fortunately, we managed to implement this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us see an order that is linked to this one. It is Exhibit D387, Defence Exhibit 387.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So D387 was written on the 16th of September, 1993, written by the command of the 2nd Battalion from Bila, and it says: "Further to the order of the Vitez Brigade command, number 01-1137-2/93, and in connection with the prevention of reckless behaviour on the part of individuals in the treatment of captured wounded enemy soldiers, I hereby order: 1. Abusing and assaulting wounded enemy soldiers who have been captured and are currently receiving treatment at our hospitals is most strictly forbidden. 2. Immediately report to the operative on duty in the 2nd Battalion or the operative on duty in the Vitez Brigade all cases of failure to comply with this order and to seek assistance from the 7th Military Police Battalion commander in Vitez by calling him on the telephone number 711-308. 3. Inform all members of our units of the contents of this order through subordinate commanders. 4. This order comes into effect immediately, and company commanders are responsible to me for its full implementation. "The command of the 2nd Battalion, Zarko Saric." Tell us, General, is there any link between these two orders, D384, I think it was, and D387?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There is. The main points of the order have almost been copied, but in this case, the battalion commander is referring to an order that he received from the Vitez Brigade, and clearly, through the system of the chain of command, document 384 was passed down to the grassroots level, that is, the soldiers, and this order was to be conveyed to all soldiers regarding the attitude they should take towards captured and wounded soldiers of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go back to your chronology of events. On the 11th of September, you were preparing the attack on the Sljibcica hill. What happened on the 12th of September?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 12th of September at about 7.30, the operations started on feature 529, Sljibcica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. The legal officer showed me that the number 592 was placed on the map. Which is the correct marking, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be best for me to look at the map, if possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, would you use the microphone because of the transcript? What is the elevation of that hill?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed. The operation started about 7.30 and it lasted until the morning at 8.55. I then issued an order for halting the operation and we stopped the operation because, at the very beginning, the operation did not produce the results that we had expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, at the 592 point on Mount Sljibcica, what was it? Was it a village or something else?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was a completely regulated position where air defence weapons were installed of 20-millimetre calibre, at times there was a tank too, and also some sniper rifles, and this position provided control over the area to the south towards the main Vitez-to-Busovaca road, and this was a classical regulated point of resistance for a unit of a strengthened platoon, possibly a company. In the immediate vicinity was the command post of the 2nd Battalion of the 325th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Of which army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, were there any civilian dwellings and civilians there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The only other thing there was a electricity pillar which was destroyed by the BH army, and later we had a lot of difficulty putting it up again because it was a long distance electricity pillar. On the 13th of September, 1993, I received information from the International Red Cross that 70 Croat civilians from Fojnica had been released and that they had been dispatched to Kiseljak. On the 14th of September, 1993, I asked for information about the loss of the position at Prosje, which is on the Busovaca front line, which we had lost several days previously. On the 16th of September, 1993, I had a great deal of difficulty in the Travnik Brigade where there was a split again within the brigade ranks and a division into two groups within the brigade. On the 18th of September, 1993, I was visited by the commander or, rather, an officer of the British battalion of UNPROFOR who was a Major by rank, and he expressed his gratitude for our cooperation and respect of UNPROFOR forces during the Grbavica operation. That same day, I was visited by representatives of the European Monitoring Mission, and they thanked us for our cooperation, the cooperation of the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone in the execution of their mission. In the course of the day, I asked that the head of operations prepare a summary review for me of all requests and responses to those requests which we had addressed to the assistant for security, including all requests in connection with the investigation in the village of Ahmici. About 23.00, I went to visit the hospital in Nova Bila, and I visited about 80 wounded in that church-cum-hospital, and on the 19th of September, 1993, there was an artillery and infantry attack on the defence lines in Vitez, that is, the front line of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the front lines remain unchanged?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they did not. The positions had moved from Zabrdze towards the explosives factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The question is: Did you gain or lose territory?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We lost territory. Urgently during the night, at 22.00, I had a meeting with the commanders of the southern sector, the villages of Donja Veceriska, and with me was Colonel Filipovic and other associates, and this was one of the more dramatic situations that we had because we couldn't find out where our positions were in this southern part of the front. There was a meeting at which we discussed the current situation, the reaction towards orders, the great fatigue felt by the personnel, and at that meeting I requested that all commanders leave their offices and that our place was to be with our soldiers in the trenches, on the front lines where our positions were. That is when we divided up the sector. A part was taken over by Colonel Filipovic and a part by me. Actually, the part towards the explosives factory from Zabrdze was within my zone, and the area from Kruscica towards Stari Vitez was in the zone of responsibility of the commander of the Vitez Brigade, who was always given a part of the front line. He was more or less the commander of a 300-metre long front line. That night my associates and myself spent together with our soldiers in the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, please, when you forbade your officers to remain in their offices, now, your headquarters, your offices, how far away was that from the front line?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the headquarters in the Hotel Vitez was never further away or nearer than 150 metres from the first sniper positions of the BH army, and Marko Prskalo and Zoran Pilicic lost their lives in that way coming back from negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: For us to be able to understand the situation better in your pocket, can you tell us, when you have a classical front, what is the depth of the deployment of a brigade and after how many kilometres does the territory where civilians are located begin, according to the military doctrine that you were taught?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The depth of brigade deployment is a minimum of 12 kilometres from the first front line, and depending on the terrain and the type of brigade, it can be up to 35 kilometres of the front with the proviso that the command post of the command of the brigade on the defence is usually behind the deployment of the forces of the first echelon which would mean a minimum of 6 kilometres from the first front line. That, as I say, is according to the rules and regulations of the former JNA, but that is approximately the same in every other army. Of course, there are always exceptions, but that is the general rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As a rule, in the zone of combat activities on the front, are civilians allowed to be there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In classical warfare, that should not be the case, civilians should not be there, located there, but the question is whether there are any other options open and what the circumstances are, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If we look at the northern front, that is, the one up above Ahmici running towards Zenica, what was the breadth of the front and the depth of your units, that is, in the rear? How many metres would you had to have gone to reach the second southern front?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it was a minimum of 1.000 metres which means that it was less than a company engaged in defence because a company has one thousand and a half -- 1.000 to 1.500 metres in depth and the maximum was 6.000 metres which means one battalion in defence. I am counting 6.000 from the northern front line to the southern front line, and all rules generally provide for the fact that behind you, you are leaning on the forces of the same army, not hostile enemy forces, but this, of course, was fighting within a total encirclement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: According to military definition, the entire pocket, did it represent the first zone of combat activities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue. What happened next, according to the chronology of events, and what events were important for us?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Already on the 20th of September, the assistant for information informed me that Radio Zenica had broadcast a news item according to which a new commander had taken command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, he had been appointed, and that I was relieved of my duties. The new commander, over the radio, the name that was read out, was Zuti, and they said that he had taken over command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. In general, the information put out -- there were rumours, and this kind of information spread across the Lasva Valley, and we had to deny these rumours and say that they were not true. At the position at Donja Veceriska, I once again had a meeting with my co-workers, the ones that I could invite to the meeting, to discuss the situation on the battleground, and my command post was to be Gornja and Donja Veceriska from then on. I was no longer in the Vitez Hotel but was in the villages right up by the front line. My associates also had their command posts in the individual sectors of the defence line. On the 21st of September, 1993, Vitez was attacked and an operation was unleashed which continued for five days, four to five nights, and the BH army attacked with its artillery and with its tanks and it was a very severe attack. In the course of the 21st of September alone, on the Lazine feature, which is in the Krizancevo Selo area, almost 300 projectiles fell, artillery mortar and other projectiles launched by the BH army, and we lost these positions north of Krizancevo Selo towards Tolovici. In the course of the day, I said that in Busovaca, a false attack should be launched on the lines of the BH army so as to alleviate the Vitez positions, particularly when we had lost our positions at Lazine and Krizancevo Selo, and I went there myself personally and I saw the commander of the 2nd Battalion from the Busovaca Brigade on that day. He wasn't able to move around, he was on crutches. He was severely wounded in both legs, but he refused to lie in hospital. He told me that he was still in command of his battalion although he could only move around on crutches, and that is what the commander of that battalion -- that was his state of health, but he remained at the front. On the 22nd of September, 1993, at 11.10, Hotel Vitez was hit again by an artillery projectile, and there were some wounded people in the Vitez Hotel. At 15.40, I received information from the Military Intelligence Service that UNPROFOR was bringing into the village of Radojcici some crates for the army of BH, and they were crates containing ammunition. I also asked for a meeting on that day with the officials of SIS, Darko Kraljevic and Miso Mijic, and they informed me once again that they were autonomous and independent in their activities and that they were not going to give any reports or be accountable to me, answerable to me for their actions. I issued a written order because of the lack of ammunition, the shortage of ammunition, to all commanders up at the front line, requesting that they only open fire -- that single firing should take place, single bullets. We had difficulty with reinforcements at the Vitez battleground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. It's been interpreted. When you say "single firing" or "single bullets," what is another -- the opposite term, that is, a burst of gunfire which can be continuous, you can have a longer or shorter burst of gunfire, but it means that you are going to use more ammunition when firing in that particular fashion. Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the course of those days, we had a great deal of difficulty with attempts to bring reinforcements to the front line in Vitez, that is to say, soldiers from the neighbouring brigades, because at the Vitez battleground, lives were being lost most, and nobody wanted to go there, to go to that front line, so that we had a great deal of problems with respect to supplying reinforcements. We also located a howitzer belonging to the BH army, 105-millimetre calibre, which acted from the Krpeljic feature. On the 23rd of September, 1993, I received information from the head of the Military Intelligence Service that five buses had arrived from Zenica to Poculica and that they were reinforcements, that fresh forces were being brought in by the BH army. I also received information from the Military Intelligence Service that, in Kruscica, a further 120 soldiers had arrived; that is to say, one entire company. On the 23rd of September, I requested from the security service that an investigation be carried out with regard to the damage done to the mosque in Busovaca, and I was informed that the damage to the mosque occurred on the 21st of September, 1993. I received information about this later on and was told that unidentified perpetrators had carried this out and that the organs of the civilian police had conducted an investigation --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What had these unidentified perpetrators done?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, there was arson in the mosque in Busovaca, fire was planted there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was there an intervention?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was informed that the fire brigade was called out and that it intervened and that the civilian police dealt with this case further.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it able to identify the perpetrators? Were they found?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not informed whether the civilian police found the perpetrators of that act or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 12.50 in the course of the day I received information, according to which the BH army was said to be preparing an attack on the Zabrdze Mountain with the probable aim of continuing on towards the explosives factory, and that is the southern position, south-lying position dominant above the explosives factory. I invited the commander, who was at the front line, I called him and cautioned him, warned him of the intentions of the BH army, and he informed me that the situation was under his control and that the situation was very stable where he was, and we even managed to tape the conversation between the commander of the BH army who envisaged that they would be taking over Zabrdze up until 14.00 on the 23rd of September, 1993. After a certain amount of time had elapsed, at about 16.30, the commander of the HVO from the Zabrdze feature asked for assistance and reinforcement for his defence, and at about 16.38, I received information that the position had been lost and that 68 soldiers belonging to the HVO had withdrawn from their positions below Mount Zabrdze. I succeeded, in the course of the afternoon, to send reinforcements but a very small number of them. First of all, I sent 12 soldiers, and then later on about 15 soldiers at about 20.15. At 22.00 on that same day, the 7th Muslim Brigade attacked the village, that is to say, the positions of the HVO in front of the village of Jardol and the village of Krcevine, which is the northern front line, and that attack was refuted, repelled. On the 24th of September, 1993, I was also situated at the Donja Veceriska command post, and I received an order coming from the main staff of the HVO, urgently to go to the headquarters to attend a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before you go to that meeting, the first outside the enclave, perhaps we can take a break, if the President agrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. We're going to have a 15-minute break, and we will finish at 5.30. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, sometime around 24 September, you went to Herzegovina on an order. To whom did you report there? What was it all about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received an order to report to the chief of the main staff of the HVO, and sometime in the evening, I went by helicopter, and at around 20.30, I met with the chief of the main staff, who at that time had his office in Citluk. There, I reported to the chief of the main staff, and I reported on the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber, for us who are following the trial here, the chief of the main staff was Brigadier Petkovic; was that the person with whom you talked?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I talked to the new chief of the main staff of the HVO. This was General Praljak. At that time, that is, on the 24th of September, General Petkovic was deputy chief of staff of the HVO, and I do not know exactly when this substitution was made, General Praljak for Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Move on. What did you talk about with him there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I informed him about the military situation and the defence issues, the problems relative to the investigation. I told him that I had given the assistant for security a final deadline of the 30th of September for the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What investigation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The investigation of Ahmici. I asked that he lend support to this deadline so that the investigation may be completed by that time, that he intervene with his superiors. I also informed him on the reorganisation of the military police, on the problems which we had with the SIS and the assistant for security in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and about the problems relating to the special purpose units who were very selective in carrying out my orders, that is, they carried out my orders in a manner which they saw fit without my being able to influence the manner in which those orders were carried out. I also suggested that these special purpose units be placed under my direct command, just as the military police units had been, and that they too be reorganised, that they dissolved and that a special unit be established which would be under the direct command of the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. After this meeting, I asked the chief of the main staff to allow me to visit my family. I was given this permission, and I went to visit my son and my wife in Austria, in Kapfenberg, where my son was staying with my in-laws. At that time, my wife was also temporarily staying with them, and my son was already going to kindergarten.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Austria?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I stayed there until the 27th of September. On the 28th of September, I came back to Citluk, and I waited for an opportunity to be taken by helicopter back to Central Bosnia, that is, to Vitez. I had another meeting with the chief of the main staff there, and in that meeting, I was informed that for several months, the forward main post had already been there for several months and that the Operative Zone in Kiseljak was directly linked to the main HVO staff as its forward command post. We also discussed some logistics issues, and I thought that that was some of the best assistance I would get in the defence of the Lasva pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How was the logistic assistance to be delivered to you when you were in this Lasva pocket?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was to have been parachuted from an aeroplane or from a helicopter, and for a helicopter, that would have been a very high altitude, because the ground was controlled by the BH army, for the most part, and the helicopter had to fly at an altitude of about 3.000 to 3.500 metres, which decreased the accuracy of drops. So some of the ordnance would have actually been dropped to the area controlled by the BH army. Another mode of assistance, but this came only later, was to land helicopters in an improvised heliodrom, but that was only during night-time, and one needed very skilful pilots because it was a very complex manoeuvre for a helicopter to land from 4.000 metres to an area which was somewhat sheltered from the possible operation of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you, at that time, get any special authority over the special purpose units during this conversation with General Praljak?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not given any authority, but I was given some promises that General Praljak was going to convey these requests, in other words, that he was going to work on my getting such authority from the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When did you come back to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I came back on the 29th of September by helicopter, and I had a meeting with the deputy commander, that is, my second in command, Mr. Filip Filipovic, in the Hotel Vitez. He informed me about the events which had taken place during my absence, including that the positions at Zabrdze had been lost, that is, the HVO positions there, that in Stari Vitez on the 26th of September, 1993, a humanitarian organisation and media representatives from the areas controlled by the BH army had visited, also that the chief of security of the explosives factory had blocked the entire compound because he had not received any cigarettes to distribute among his employees. In other words, it was again a wilful act on the part of this security officer. There was a conflict between the assistant for security, Mr. Sliskovic, and the deputy chief of the centre of security, Mr. Kraljevic. Also that there was shooting in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say "Kraljevic," this is Darko Kraljevic, the former commander of the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I was informed by Mr. Filipovic, that also there was shooting in Vitez, and that Mr. Dario Kordic, Mr. Ignjac Kostroman, and Mr. Anto Sliskovic, assistant for security, visited Darko Kraljevic, but they were not allowed to leave Vitez, in other words, that they were released by him only after a call had come in from Mr. Mate Boban and personally ordered Kraljevic to release Mr. Dario Kordic as well as Messrs. Ignjac Kostroman and Anto Sliskovic, but Darko Kraljevic forbid them to return to the town of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, you said that Darko Kraljevic had basically taken Dario Kordic prisoner. Can you tell the Chamber what Dario Kordic's post or duty was in Central Bosnia in 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was the vice-president of the HDZ for Central Bosnia, and he was the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. This, as far as I know, were the two positions which he held.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does that mean that Dario Kordic was Mate Boban's deputy?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What duty did Ignjac Kostroman have in 1993, that is, the second person taken prisoner by Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was the secretary-general of the Croatian Democratic Community, and I think that he was on that duty both in 1992 and 1993; in other words, he was the secretary-general of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this only for Central Bosnia or for the entire Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was for the HDZ in the entire Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And the third person who was detained by Darko Kraljevic was Anto Sliskovic. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was assistant for security with the Central Bosnia Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In other words, are you saying the chief of SIS?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he was the chief of the SIS for the Central Bosnia Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: He said that Mate Boban had intervened so that the three of them would be released.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, so that they would be released and they would be permitted to leave the town of Vitez. Mato Boban's intervention was for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know whether anything happened to Darko Kraljevic? Was he arrested? Was he tried for this abduction, if you will, of three very high-level functionaries of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was not tried and no proceedings were instituted against him for this act.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: My mind may have strayed a while, General, so do forgive me in case you did explain this. Tell me, did you have any understanding at the time as to why Darko Kraljevic abducted these people, Kordic and others?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the time I had just returned from Herzegovina and I was briefed about it by my deputy. I did not have any knowledge then nor do I know today what was the real motive for such behaviour and why he did that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: During the three days you went to Austria, nobody told you about your command, there were no telephone contacts with these people?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, for those three days, my deputy stood in for me, so I didn't have any contact because I was on a family visit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Even while you were with your family during a time of war, you were not wondering -- you were not saying to the people at the command post, "If there is something urgent, maybe you could call me?" You leave three days without any contact?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I never left without leaving all my telephone numbers to my deputy where he could find me, if necessary, and at any point in time, he was able to contact me, of course, if the lines were open. He knew where I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [interpretation cuts in] ... reassure me, because you said a moment ago that you were a professional soldier, and I was very surprised that you could leave a war without leaving any number. Now, my question is: Did your deputy do a good job by not telling you what was going on while Mr. Kostroman, Mr. Sliskovic, and the other person were arrested? It was not a minor event, was it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He informed the chief of the main staff and Mr. Mato Boban probably, since Mate Boban was the one who intervened. He did not inform me personally when that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, would there have been any point if you had been informed? Could you order Darko Kraljevic to release Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could issue such an order, and even after Mr. Mate Boban issued the order, Dario Kordic was issued an order by Darko Kraljevic that he could not return to Vitez. Therefore, judging by his reaction to Mr. Mate Boban's order, it is clear that he didn't even fully respect his order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me the difference between your authority over Darko Kraljevic and the authority of Mate Boban; was there any difference?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The difference is vast. I was equal in rank to Colonel Darko Kraljevic, and the difference was vast between Mate Boban and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In whose favour?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Mate Boban's favour because he was also the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you consider that Colonel Filip Filipovic acted correctly by not calling you in Austria but, rather, calling Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It would have been better if Colonel Filipovic had called me up at least to let me know that this had happened, but I believe that he realised that his capacity to deal with the problem was equal to his own, and in his effort to deal with it as quickly as possible, he probably contacted the main chief of staff who then contacted Mr. Mate Boban. But it would have been a good thing if I had at least been informed so I would know what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go on then. You had some other meetings with UNPROFOR representatives?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This was probably in the afternoon. I had a meeting with Colonel Duncan and Colonel Williams who was announced as the new commander of the British UNPROFOR battalion based in Nova Bila and we discussed daily matters. This was more like a courtesy visit because it was my first encounter with Colonel Williams. There were questions also related to difficulties in the passage of convoys towards Stari Vitez and Kruscica. When I say "difficulties," I mean the behaviour of Croatian civilians who demonstrated their suspicion that those convoys were transporting ammunition for the needs of the BH army, and they demanded that their representative participate in inspecting the freight which could be done at any location. Then Colonel Williams also inquired into the situation in Zepce, Kiseljak, Vares, and I said that occasionally we were in touch and that I had some general information but that I was not aware of the detailed situation and I was not informed about all developments. We also discussed electricity, because Vitez was most of the time without electricity, then also the question of the shortage of water for Novi Travnik, the church-cum-hospital and the whole town of Vitez, and also problems related to the evacuation of the wounded from the church-cum-hospital. In the afternoon, I received information after this meeting from the chief of staff on the situation on our positions north of the town of Vitez on the front lines. I was also informed by the assistant for information that rumours were spreading in Vitez and they were being spread by Mr. Darko Kraljevic that Central Bosnia had been sold out and that there was no point to continue the struggle for survival in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, General, these stories that Central Bosnia had been sold out, by whom and for what purpose and to whom? Could you explain that a little?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These were rumours that were circulating in Central Bosnia, that there would be a swap of territories, that the whole of Mostar would belong to Herceg-Bosna and Central Bosnia -- to Herzegovina and the Croats, that is, Mostar, whereas Central Bosnia would be given to the Bosniak Muslims and that there was no purpose to continue the struggle for our presence in the Lasva pocket as, in any event, all of it would be in the hands of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Those rumours, what was their effect on the morale of your combatants?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They certainly had an effect and they undermined the confidence of the soldiers because if people were getting killed on a daily basis, then soldiers asked themselves: What was the purpose of getting killed and trying to defend this territory if it would in any event fall into the hands of the attacker? Why risk one's life? Why struggle then? We had difficulties in calming down and stabilising the situation and rejecting those rumours as unfounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you, by any chance, know how come Darko Kraljevic had such information when you and your soldiers did not have it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He, at the time, held two high-ranking positions, commander of the special purpose unit and deputy chief of the security centre, so that he was directly subordinate to the defence department and he probably had access to high-level sources of information, although I don't know on what grounds he had that information nor where the source was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 29th of September, the assistant for security of the 1st Battalion was killed, that is, Mr. Ivan Budimir, he was killed by an unidentified perpetrator, and Mr. Ivan Budimir was very well-known as a special person who opposed crime and all criminal activities, especially in his capacity as assistant for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us: Ivan Budimir, is that the same Ivan Budimir whose reports we read at the beginning of your testimony and they had to do with the end of 1992, the beginning of 1993, when he reported that the arrival of units from Herzegovina had raised to boiling point the inter-ethnic relations between Croats and Muslims; is that the same man?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes it is, assistant for security of the 1st Battalion of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 30th of September, 1993, I asked the assistant for security to report to me about the investigation into the crime in Ahmici, and he informed me that the whole complete file, including the names of the suspects of the crime in Ahmici, had been handed over to the competent administration for security and that it was no longer my concern because they had taken over the whole file, the whole case. In the course of that day, Darko Kraljevic fired, in the town of Vitez, from a heavy machine gun, about 600 bullets, and his superior, the head of the security services, took control of the ammunitions factory and prohibited entry into the factory to all persons, including myself, declaring that as of the 30th of September, the centre of the security services was taking over the ammunition factory under its control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, General, what was the name of the head of the Security and Information Service who was superior to Mr. Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: His name was Mr. Miso Mijic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Before adjourning, I would like to ask you two questions, General: The investigation about Ahmici, you were told that you had nothing to do with it anymore, and you said, "Okay, I will not deal with it anymore." You were a very disciplined soldier then. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that point in time, Mr. President, when I was told that the entire case had been completed and the names of the suspects had been handed over to the security administration, I felt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Were you not asking any questions to learn the conclusions of the investigation then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I asked the assistant for security whether the whole file was complete --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's an official request. But that's not my question. There is no point in going further. I understood that you were not dealing with the investigation anymore; am I right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did concern myself with that matter later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But you think that it is not part of your duties in your chain of command. The second observation, which is linked to the first one, relates to Darko Kraljevic. You are a very disciplined soldier within the chain of command. Ahmici, you have explained to us, was not in your chain of command, that it's not part of your duties, and this is the conclusion that you have on the 30th of September, 1993, a report has been written, and you have nothing to do with it anymore; and since you are a disciplined soldier, you say, "This is not part of my chain of command and I shall not deal with this anymore." My question relates to Darko Kraljevic. During the various days before the 30th of September, Mr. Darko Kraljevic is guilty of a disciplinary mistake because one of his deputies shoots at a factory. I think it's one of his deputies; right? No? It's not one of his deputies? I thought that 600 bullets were fired, but on what? Did I misunderstand you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, he fired in town 600 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, okay. I'm trying to link two different points of view, two different ways of seeing the chain of command. When you are a subordinate, you're a very disciplined soldier. The army chief is an example. This concerned military security, and this had nothing to do, you agree. But when we have to deal with Mr. Darko Kraljevic, he is acting in your zone of responsibility, he is intervening in the operations by shooting 600 bullets, while you are yourself in a very complex situation from a military point of view and, at the same time, he was bringing down the morale of the troops by saying that Bosnia would be sold out. My question is therefore the following: You have just met General Praljak, he is the new chief of staff, so do you tell this General, "This is enough. Either you keep Kraljevic or I will resign"? Did you think about saying this to General Praljak?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I informed the chief of the main staff of what I had achieved with the reorganisation of the military police, and I told him that I asked that the same model be applied to the special purpose units, including Mr. Darko Kraljevic. However, Darko Kraljevic was not only the commander of that unit but he had been promoted in the hierarchy; he was also deputy head of the security centre, over which I had absolutely no jurisdiction. So he held two very high-level positions attached to the defence ministry. I did ask for that but, Mr. President, these incidents did not occur before my visit for me to be able to react to them, but I received even this information through an investigation and a report on it submitted to me by the assistant for security about the incident in town. Everything I learnt I forwarded to the main chief of staff, and I managed to achieve the disbanding of the special purpose unit and the forming of a guards unit directly subordinated to me, but this took time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I've understood that, but I have the feeling that, in fact, whenever there is a chain of command above you, whatever the situation, you decide not to say anything. Can I interpret your testimony like this: Whenever you have a chief or a superior above you, whenever you're in a situation in which you are part of a chain of command, and above you someone tells you, "This is the way things should be," because you are a subordinate, then you choose not to act, whatever the situation is.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I sought to respect everything, but, Mr. President, even in this situation, when I received the information from the assistant for security on the report into the investigation in Ahmici, I did not give up my efforts to discover whether criminal proceedings had been instituted or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's all. Are there any other questions? Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, this assistant for security was superior to you or subordinate to you or did he hold a parallel position?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, he was directly subordinate to the administration for security, and he would service my requests, which means that I could make requests to him, but his vertical chain of command, as we saw on the schematic, was the administration for security in Mostar, and the orders of that administration had absolute priority over any requests that I may have made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: One final question. I gather that you considered that the rumours being spread by Darko Kraljevic about a possible exchange of territories were unfounded. Did you gather why Darko Kraljevic was spreading about those rumours?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did my best to stabilise their will for defence among my soldiers, believing that, in such a situation, those rumours were unfounded, but, Your Honour, I don't know whether Darko Kraljevic got such information from because there was a big difference between me and Darko Kraljevic in relation to the Defence Ministry. Above Darko Kraljevic, there is the Defence Ministry on two grounds, as deputy head of security and information and as head of the brigade. So I never managed to establish whether those rumours had any grounds or not. I personally felt that they were unfounded because our priority was to retain our presence there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I think tomorrow we will resume at 9.00, since it's Friday. Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 5.37 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 26th day of March, 1999, at 9.00 a.m.
